edgeDifference: Legacy selects in place on its loaded layer; next applies NextFlattenSession.setVariantOverride before begin(). The three-argument form maps to a prim-scoped key ("<prim>{<set>}"); the one-argument form, which legacy forces on every variant set, maps to one set-name override per set.

An idle call cancels nothing on either product; legacy records it as cancelRequested in its progress record, next does not. Next additionally reports and controls a running parse from the RenderStream progress callback; legacy loads synchronously without a JS callback and has no equivalent. Called from the callback it cancels the load (stage "cancelled").

Next authors every legacy attribute with the same values (URDF prim hierarchy, meshes, joints, collider purpose=guide, Newton scene settings and MuJoCo/Newton contact and mesh-collision attributes and APIs) and additionally authors mjc:timestep and mjc:contype/conaffinity.

knownDifference: Next product contract: failures report the next parser's located message ("Line N, column M: ..."); legacy reports its own parser error stack. Empty-string results for idle and successful loads match.

edgeDifference: Both rewrite the root layer's asset path; next packages the asset under the remapped name, while legacy keeps the original entry name and leaves the remapped reference dangling.
Next keeps mesh geometry arrays (points, faceVertexCounts, faceVertexIndices) in the stage export; legacy loses those the converter consumed. All other content matches.

knownDifference: Both describe the same prims in the same order, but next's physics JSON is its own contract: schema fallback properties and geometry arrays instead of legacy's specifier/flag/matrix fields and point/face counts.

Next lists authored texture asset paths that did not resolve (for example shader.usda's 0/teapot_*.png); legacy returns an empty list for those. Resolved textures agree. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

edgeDifference: A zero-length stream cannot be finalized in legacy; next finalizes it as an empty asset.
Next keeps a referenced layer's relative asset path as authored (@old.png@) where legacy re-anchors it (@./old.png@), per next's relative-asset-path policy.
Bone textures are identical for bound meshes; next also skins a mesh that binds a skeleton without applying SkelBindingAPI, which legacy leaves unskinned.

knownDifference: Includes next's additional PortalLight/filter records (see numLights). Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Next skeletal animations are array channels (valueStride/elementCount/jointRemap) rather than legacy per-joint tracks; clips are named "<name>_Anim" and carry primPath/startTime/endTime instead of legacy value-clip metadata. Custom-property values match legacy. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Next reports one channel per skeletal animation (legacy one track per joint TRS), names clips after the source prim ("<name>_Anim"), counts the skeleton node as a target, and exposes startTime/endTime instead of legacy value-clip fields. duration matches (last key time). Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

edgeDifference: Default spelling differs: legacy reports "./", next reports the resolver working directory "."; set/get round-trips match.

knownDifference: Next camera records use primPath, type/typeCode, fovX/fovY, nearClip/farClip, aperture offsets, exposure, focus, fStop, shutter and stereo fields plus the transform; legacy uses absPath/displayName/projection/xfov/yfov/znear/zfar/aspectRatio. Shared values match. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.
Legacy defaults to combining UDIM tiles; next intentionally defaults to sparse tiles (false) for editor workflows. Setter/getter behavior is covered, but the product default differs.

Next node records add primPath/type/visible/worldMatrix/prototypePath fields and omit legacy prototypeIndex/instanceId; displayName falls back to the prim name. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Maps to getImageView: same image record contract as getImageCopy (componentType/mipLevels/name, numeric colorSpace; an undecoded image reports 0 width/height and 4 channels) with a borrowed pixel view only for decoded images. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Instance ids follow next's native-instance enumeration: records are the instancing prims with their world matrices and resolved prototype mesh ids. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Next records use primPath, enableShadow, typeCode, light-link/filter targets and type-specific shape fields; legacy adds absPath/displayName/position/direction, all shape fields with defaults, shapingConeAngle (degrees), guideRadius and texture/geometry links. Next names distant lights "directional", reports shaped sphere lights as "spot" with a radian cone angle, and includes PortalLights. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.
Legacy reports its mmap flag (false by default); next throws because next-only WASM assets are never mmap-backed (explicit product decision).

The next product uses an architecture-independent 1 GiB default; legacy defaults to 2 GiB on wasm32 and 8 GiB on memory64. Next also rejects limits outside 1..8192 MiB, while legacy preserves signed integer values. This is an intentional untrusted-input safety policy difference.

edgeDifference: Mesh, material, texture, image, light and asset counts match; node, buffer and cache-byte fields report each product's own accounting.

knownDifference: Next returns borrowed heap descriptors ({ptr,length,comps,dtype}) for geometry, a non-indexed triangle soup, primPath/localMatrix/worldMatrix/material, and an unbound mesh uses the fallback material id; legacy returns indexed typed arrays with face counts/uvSets/normalsFormat. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Owned copies of next's non-indexed geometry (uv0, vertexCount, local/world matrices, material); legacy returns indexed arrays with face counts, uvSets and packed normals. An unbound mesh uses the fallback material id. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Next reports every primvar of the retained mesh (legacy returned an empty set for the interpolation fixture) and omits legacy's "render node is not a GeomMesh" error for plain meshes. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Maps to getMeshGeometryView: f32 geometry views plus skin/bind-transform and matrix fields; legacy returns indexed descriptors (snorm8 normals, faceVertexCounts, submesh flags). Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Next product contract: the record tracks each load (stage "complete"/"error"/"cancelled", byte counts, errorMessage equal to error()). Legacy reports stage "idle" with "Conversion complete" after loading, keeps that record after a failed parse, and keeps cancelRequested set after an idle cancelParsing(). Idle records match.

Same node record contract as getDefaultRootNode: next adds primPath/type/visible/worldMatrix/prototypePath, omits prototypeIndex/instanceId, and falls back to the prim name for displayName. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

Next adds primPath/joints/rootJoint/jointCount/animationSourcePath; skeleton ids follow next's traversal order (legacy orders them differently) and joint names are leaf names instead of full joint paths. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.

joint_names are leaf joint names in next and full joint paths in legacy; other arrays match. Next RenderStream record shape is the product contract; the exact field differences are pinned in next-render-scene-contract.json.
